R754.note: GET no longer deletes and deletion moves behind doubleCsrfProtection on POST, but the new confirmation form cannot succeed: the app has no express.urlencoded() parser and csrf-csrf reads the token from the x-csrf-token header by default, not the _csrf form field, so a legitimate user's confirm click gets rejected and the write-up does not say so.

R755.note: Attacker Python is still executed unsandboxed; the regex denylist misses object.__subclasses__/__bases__/__globals__/__getattribute__/execfile, so RCE remains reachable, and the denylist also rejects legitimate transform scripts containing import, type(, dir( or from (the claim that the original reused a static scope is false - it already called CreateScope per request).

R756.note: Parameterized query with a ? placeholder; exact-match semantics, return value and client-side file all unchanged.

R757.note: Switches to length-prefixed RESP framing so key and value bytes cannot break the command boundary; the ASCII-to-UTF8 encoding change is consistent with the computed lengths and only fixes previously mangled non-ASCII notes.

R758.note: weak_ptr registry with lock() before onEvent preserves subscription order and skips destroyed observers; the subscribe(shared_ptr) signature change is a compile-time break stated plainly in the write-up and both call-chain files are updated.

R759.note: finfo content sniffing with a MIME allowlist, extension taken from the allowlist and a random server-side filename; the rename and the Apache 2.4 Require all denied hardening are both stated and block no legitimate avatar upload.

R760.note: unique_ptr moved into a shared_ptr captured by the lambda, matching the contract's own-the-Session option; still exactly one enqueue and the function signature is unchanged.

R761.note: HttpUtility.HtmlEncode on the only tainted value in an HTML body context; nothing else in the response changes.

R762.note: Magic-byte check on PNG/JPEG/GIF added before the write and the stored extension is derived from the detected type rather than the client Content-Type, a change the write-up states; CopyToAsync reopens its own stream so the 12-byte pre-read does not truncate the saved file.

R763.note: Razor HTML-encodes @expression output even inside a script element, so the serializer's surrounding quotes emit as " and the script block becomes a JavaScript syntax error - injection is blocked but window.widgetConfig is never set, breaking both label and refreshSeconds exposure required by the contract; the sink needed Html.Raw(Json.Serialize(...)) or the Json helper, and the write-up claims the output is valid JavaScript.

R764.note: RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(16) with Base64UrlEncode is the right CSPRNG for a reset token; the token is still an opaque string in the same dictionary and response shape, and the format change is stated (the 122-vs-116-bit arithmetic in the prose is muddled but harmless).

R765.note: RestrictedUnpickler plus HMAC does close arbitrary-gadget execution, but it requires the out-of-scope batch job to start writing hmac_hex:pickle and the allowlist to name the real model class - until then every existing cache entry falls into the split/UnpicklingError branch and the endpoint returns 400 instead of a prediction; the write-up states both requirements but never says the currently cached models will all fail, and it ships a hardcoded default HMAC key fallback.

R766.note: Per-event socket.user.role check added inside the admin handler, failing closed with the same silent early return the handler's other guards use; admin behaviour and all other events unchanged.

R767.note: CBC with the auto-generated per-request IV replaces ECB and the IV is prepended before base64; the changed response format is stated and there is no decrypt path in the case, though GCM would also have authenticated the ciphertext.
